blindSourceSummaries: A foreign government's country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity (June 2025): no specific law criminalises LGBT+ identity as such, but at least 139 individuals were affected by anti-LGBT+ laws including 'gay propaganda' convictions, detentions and 'extremism' prosecutions; no SOGI discrimination legislation; the note's central distinction is that general state risk is not established across the country except in a restive peripheral region, and it notes there is no reliable data on the size or distribution of the LGBT+ population.

An international human-rights organisation (30 June 2025): courts issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participation in or display of symbols of an alleged 'international LGBT movement'; repeated display of a banned symbol carries up to four years' imprisonment; cases include forced labour after posting a rainbow flag on social media, and administrative sentences that prompted users to delete accounts out of fear of prosecution.
